m2c/tests/tools/conftest.py -- Patch C05: shared fixtures for the tool tests.

* ``proj``, ``ctx`` and ``outside`` come from tools_fixtures.py (the helpers
  themselves are imported by name in each module).
* ``caplog`` is wrapped so it still sees the ``m2c`` logger after another test
  module has called ``configure_logging()`` (which turns propagation off, so
  pytest's root-logger handler would otherwise capture nothing).  The handler
  is attached to the ``m2c`` logger directly and propagation is held off for the
  duration, so each record is captured exactly once either way.

m2c/tests/tools/test_tools_files.py -- Patch C05: read_file, list_dir,
edit_file, write_file and delete_path (m2c.tools.files), driven through
``run_tool`` so the argument validation and the result shape are exercised too.

Groups, in file order:

* read_file       line ranges, truncation marker, binary / non-UTF-8 refusal,
                  FIFOs, huge files, the "seen" record.
* list_dir        caps, symlink marks, depth, hidden protected entries.
* edit_file       unique / missing / non-unique matches, diff, read-before-edit.
* write_file      read-before-write, changed-since-read, atomic replace, mode,
                  parent directories, final-symlink refusal.
* interrupted     fault injection at os.replace / os.fsync / os.write, a real
  writes          child killed with SIGKILL between the temp write and the
                  rename, stale temp cleanup, and the concurrent-change check.
* races           a component swapped for a symlink between check and open.
* delete_path     files, empty / non-empty / recursive directories, the root,
                  .git, symlinks.

Run: cd m2c && pytest tests/tools/test_tools_files.py -v

m2c/tests/tools/test_tools_paths.py -- Patch C05: the path guard and the
two-form denylist (m2c.tools.paths).

The 14 tests ported from the daemon are in test_tools_path_guard_port.py; this
file is everything C05 adds: traversal and absolute paths, NUL bytes, symlink
escapes for reads, writes and deletes, the "never follow a symlink for the
final component of a write" rule, sibling-prefix names, over-broad roots, the
hard-coded denylist (every entry, case-insensitively, evaluated before the
filesystem is touched), the user denylist (pattern forms, validation, and that
it can never loosen the hard list), and the race between checking a path and
opening it (a component swapped for a symlink in between must be refused, not
followed).

Run: cd m2c && pytest tests/tools/test_tools_paths.py -v

m2c/tests/tools/test_tools_run_tool.py -- Patch C05: the executor entry point
(``m2c.tools.run_tool``) and the properties that cut across every tool.

* Dispatch fails closed: unknown tools, non-dict arguments, unknown / missing /
  mistyped / out-of-range arguments are errors, and the error never echoes the
  offending value.
* The argument table is checked against the real schemas in
  ``m2c/protocol/v1/tools/*.json`` so the two cannot drift apart silently.
* The result has the wire shape of protocol/v1 ``tool_result`` (ok, output,
  truncated, trust, duration_ms) and never exceeds the 200000-character limit.
* The hard denylist is enforced by every tool, including the three that list
  or search (their output must not even *name* a protected file).
* Logging: tool name, status, code, size and duration only; never a path,
  pattern, argument or file content, and no call site bypasses ``log_event``.

Run: cd m2c && pytest tests/tools/test_tools_run_tool.py -v

m2c/tests/tools/test_tools_search.py -- Patch C05: glob and grep
(m2c.tools.search).

glob is pure Python and is tested directly.  grep is a ripgrep wrapper, so it
is tested at three levels, because CI's m2c job has no ripgrep installed
(.github/workflows/ci.yml says so) and the security properties must not depend
on it being there:

1. ``build_rg_argv`` as a pure function: whatever text the model supplies, the
   pattern is the one token after ``-e``, the path is the one token after
   ``--``, and every other token comes from a fixed allowlist.  No ``--pre``,
   no ``--pre-glob``, no ``-f``, no shell.
2. A *fake* ``rg`` (a small Python script) that records the argument list,
   working directory and environment it was started with and prints crafted
   output: this proves the wrapper's post-filtering of protected files, its
   output caps, timeout, process cleanup and error handling without a real
   ripgrep.
3. The *real* ``rg``, skipped loudly when it is missing: flag-shaped patterns
   are searched as text and nothing is executed, ignore files and hidden files
   behave, symlinks are not followed.

Run: cd m2c && pytest tests/tools/test_tools_search.py -v

m2c/tests/tools/test_tools_shell_dispatch.py -- Patch C07: the three small,
backward-compatible changes to C05's ``m2c.tools`` entry point that the shell
tool needs, tested on their own (the shell itself is in test_tools_shell.py):

(a) ``bash`` is in ``ARG_SPECS`` (it mirrors protocol/v1/tools/bash.json; the
    parametrized schema test in test_tools_run_tool.py compares them) and in
    ``TOOLS``;
(b) ``ToolResult`` has an optional ``exit_code`` that ``to_payload`` includes
    only when it is set;
(c) ``run_tool`` takes an optional keyword-only ``call_env`` that is handed
    only to executors that declare a ``call_env`` parameter, and an executor
    may return a ``ToolOutcome`` (a result that can be a failure and still keep
    its output, trust label, exit code and a local code).

Every existing tool keeps its exact behaviour: a tool that returns the old
``(output, truncated)`` tuple is untouched.

Run: cd m2c && pytest tests/tools/test_tools_shell_dispatch.py -v

m2c/tests/tools/tools_fixtures.py -- Patch C05: shared helpers for the local
tool executor tests.

Imported by name from the test modules in this directory (the same convention
as tests/auth/auth_fixtures.py and tests/link/link_fakes.py: pytest puts a test
file's own directory on sys.path).

Nothing here looks like a real secret.  The "secret" files the tests plant are
filled with the marker ``SECRETWORD`` (or ``MARKER_*`` strings), which no
secret scanner treats as a credential, and any fake token a test needs is built
at run time (``"x" * 40``) rather than written as a literal.
